units.function: Two-line CLI adapter facade exporting registry lookup and the shared CLIAdapterModule type.
units.dependencyDirection: Consumers import inward through this local facade; the implementation delegates lookup to the CLI registry and exposes its contract from @paperclipai/adapter-utils.
units.lifecycle: Import the facade; request an adapter through registry lookup; type consumers against the shared module interface.
units.testAssessment: No focused test exists for this facade. CLI no-emit TypeScript passed on 2026-08-19. The export itself is trivial, while behavior and completeness belong to registry/adapter units.
units.designRationale: Keep consumers independent of registry file layout and centralize the public CLI adapter import path.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a narrow stable Connector SDK and separate presentation adapter facade so vendor implementations can evolve without leaking registry or runtime internals into core/application.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the narrow facade pattern only. Company OS must own its Connector contracts in connector-sdk/ports, version them explicitly and avoid re-exporting upstream/Paperclip types. CLI event formatting should remain downstream of normalized Connector projections.
units.responsibilityConflict: None in the facade itself; the risk is architectural—re-exporting an implementation-owned type can allow its incomplete identity/evidence/session semantics to become the system-wide contract.
evidence: 73eb23734f25c570d88665e672f80d740797c632 docs: use structured agent mentions in paperclip skill (#4103)
securityFindings: The facade exposes an upstream shared type as the public contract; security-critical omissions in that type can propagate to every adapter consumer.
No version/capability negotiation, structured event/evidence schema or secret-free invariant is visible at this boundary.
Registry lookup failure/unknown adapter behavior is not tested here.
Type-level separation does not enforce runtime plugin trust, provenance or sandbox policy.
